title: Ballot measure
description: One California statewide proposition or Santa Clara County ballot measure. This file is the single source of truth for the data shape: scripts/validate.mjs validates against it, so adding or changing a field means editing this file only.

id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier, also the output filename. Examples: ca-prop-1-2026, scc-measure-a-2026.

jurisdiction.description: Which ballot this measure appears on. Exactly "state" for a California statewide proposition, or "county" for a county measure.

county.description: County name without the word "County", for example "Santa Clara". Required when jurisdiction is "county", omitted otherwise.

election_date.description: Date of the election this measure is on, as YYYY-MM-DD.

number.description: Display label as voters will see it on the ballot, for example "Proposition 1" or "Measure A".

title.description: Official short title of the measure.

status.description: Where the measure sits in the qualification and election process.

summary.description: Two to three sentences of plain English describing what the measure does. Shown on the landing page card and at the top of the detail page.

what_it_really_means.description: The plain-language deep dive, one string per paragraph. This is the human-written analysis; nothing generates it.

fiscal_impact.description: The money picture, broken into the five figures voters ask about plus a narrative that ties them together.

state_cost.description: What the state pays, as a dollar figure or range, or "none".

state_savings.description: What the state stops paying, as a dollar figure or range, or "none".

local_cost.description: What cities, counties, and special districts pay, or "none".

revenue_change.description: Net change in government revenue, with direction and rough size.

ongoing_vs_one_time.description: Whether the costs and revenues above recur every year or land once.

narrative.description: Longer explanation of the fiscal picture, including what the headline numbers leave out.

taxes.description: Tax effects, separated into taxes that do not exist today and changes to taxes that do.

new_taxes.description: Taxes the measure creates. Empty array if it creates none.

tax_changes.description: Existing taxes the measure raises, lowers, extends, or redirects. Empty array if none.

spending.description: Where the money goes and where it comes from.

new_spending_areas.description: Programs or categories that receive money under the measure. Empty array if none.

funding_source.description: Where the spending is paid from: bonds, general fund, a new tax, a redirected fund.

control_and_power.description: Who gains authority, oversight, or control, and over whom. Name the body and what it can decide without further approval.

loopholes.description: Ambiguities, exemptions, and exploitable gaps in the text. Empty array if none found, but say so in the deep dive rather than leaving it unexamined.

unexpected_provisions.description: Riders and non-obvious items bundled in that a voter reading the title would not expect. Empty array if none.

pros.description: Arguments in favor, stated as a supporter would state them.

cons.description: Arguments against, stated as an opponent would state them.

who_supports.description: Named backers, with enough note to show why their support is informative.

who_opposes.description: Named opponents, with enough note to show why their opposition is informative.

authors.description: Who wrote or filed this measure: legislative authors/coauthors for a Legislature-referred measure, or proponents for an initiative. Optional.

role.description: Their role on this measure, e.g. "Lead Senate author", "Initiative proponent".

person_id.description: Optional id of a matching file in content/people/, linking this name to a full profile page. Omit if no profile exists yet.

funding.description: Money behind the campaign: registered committees, what they raised, and named donors where verifiable. Distinct from who_supports/who_opposes, which are public positions rather than money. Optional; omit entirely if no committee-finance data has been found.

nonpartisan_analysis.description: Summaries from nonpartisan analysts such as the Legislative Analyst's Office or Ballotpedia. Empty array if none published yet.

source.description: Name of the analyzing body, for example "Legislative Analyst's Office".

summary.description: What that analysis concluded, in your own words.

url.description: Link to the analysis. Must be http or https to render as a link; file: URLs and absolute paths are rejected so local machine details never get published.

sources.description: Primary sources the analysis rests on. scripts/fetch-sources.mjs archives every url listed here.

title.description: Human-readable name of the source document.

url.description: Link to the source. Must be http or https to render as a link; file: URLs and absolute paths are rejected so local machine details never get published.

retrieved.description: Date the source was read, as YYYY-MM-DD.

last_updated.description: Date this file was last edited by a human, as YYYY-MM-DD.

name.description: Name of the person or organization.

type.description: What kind of backer this is.

notes.description: Why this backer matters: funding, stake in the outcome, past positions.

committee.description: A registered ballot-measure committee raising or spending money on this measure.

total_raised.description: Total contributions, as a dollar figure or "not yet reported".

top_donors.description: Named donors with amounts, where a reliable donor-level breakdown was found. Empty array if none found — never fabricate a donor or amount.

source_url.description: Where the finance figures came from: Cal-Access, FPPC, or the committee's own filing. Never a local file path.
